reasoning: Because the plastic rods are milled and ground from sheet stock (headings 3920/3921) rather than formed in a single operation, they are classified in heading 3926. The Indian sheets undergo the required tariff shift to heading 3926 in Mexico under 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 4416 from any other heading
decisive_step: Crafting and assembling the white oak staves and steel hoops into barrels in Mexico
flip: Importing pre-made barrel staves of heading 4416 into Mexico for simple assembly
reasoning: New casks and barrels of wood are classified under heading 4416 (4416.00.3010). Under 19 CFR 102.20, heading 4416 requires a change from any other heading. Raw lumber and steel hoops shift to 4416 when handcrafted into barrels in Mexico.

key_factors: (b) single failing material imparting essential character
decisive_step: Manufacture of the receiver dryer subassembly in China
flip: Manufacture the receiver dryer subassembly in Canada or the United States
reasoning: Both the imported Chinese receiver dryer subassembly and the finished unit are classified in subheading 8421.39, failing the 102.20 tariff shift rule in Canada. Under 102.11(b)(1), the single failing material (the receiver dryer) imparts the essential character, conferring Chinese origin.

key_factors: (a)(1) wholly obtained or produced as waste and scrap in Mexico
decisive_step: Generation of gold waste, scrap, and dust from jewelry manufacturing in Mexico
flip: Generating the waste and scrap from manufacturing operations performed in the United States
reasoning: The gold waste, scrap, and polishing dust are classified under subheading 7112.91.01, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.1(g)(9), waste and scrap derived from manufacturing operations in a country are wholly obtained or produced there, conferring Mexican origin under 102.11(a)(1) (or 102.11(a)(3)).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 8433.11
decisive_step: Manufacturing components and assembling the lawn mower in Mexico
flip: Importing an incomplete mower already classified in subheading 8433.11 into Mexico for simple assembly
reasoning: Following N350133, the walk-behind lawn mower is classified in subheading 8433.11. The 102.20 rule for 8433.11-8433.59 requires a change from any other subheading, including parts of 8433.90. All foreign parts and materials shift to 8433.11 in Mexico under 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (b) single failing material imparting essential character
decisive_step: manufacture of the base belt in Taiwan
flip: Manufacture the base belt in Canada from non-heading 4010 rubber and textile materials
reasoning: The finished endless conveyor belt with vulcanized profiles remains in heading 4010 (4010.12). The 102.20 rule for heading 4010 requires a shift from any other heading. The Taiwanese base belt (4010.12) fails to shift in Canada, imparting essential character under 102.11(b).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8414.59
decisive_step: Final assembly of the fan blower components in Mexico
flip: Importing an incomplete fan assembly already classified in subheading 8414.59 into Mexico
reasoning: Unlike USMCA GN 11(o) which requires a heading change, 19 CFR 102.20 for 8414.10-8414.80 only requires a change from any other subheading. Foreign parts (housings, impeller in 8414.90, motor in 8501) shift to 8414.59 in Mexico under 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character from Chinese molded doll components
decisive_step: Molding of the ABS plastic doll components in China
flip: Molding the plastic doll components in Mexico instead of China
reasoning: The doll and its parts are classified in heading 9503.00. Under 102.20(s), heading 9503 requires a shift from any other heading. Because the Chinese parts are also in heading 9503 (or constitute an unassembled doll under 102.17(c)), they fail to shift; under 102.11(b)(1), origin is China.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 6406

flip: Using foreign footwear parts of heading 6406 that fail the tariff shift
reasoning: Removable hockey skate inserts/insoles are classified under subheading 6406.90. Assuming production occurs in Canada from non-heading 6406 materials, all foreign inputs satisfy the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 9018.90
decisive_step: Manufacturing the thermocouple subassembly and assembling the RF probe in Mexico
flip: Import pre-made RF probe under 9018.90 into Mexico for mere packaging
reasoning: The RF probe is an electro-surgical/medical instrument classified under 9018.90.6000. All foreign materials (steel hypo-tubes of Ch. 73, wires/cables of 8544, connectors of 8536, plastics of Ch. 39) are outside heading 9018 and satisfy the 102.20 tariff shift in Mexico.

key_factors: (b) essential character imparted by the toothed rings/races
decisive_step: Machining and production of the toothed slewing rings in China

reasoning: Because the slew bearings feature gear teeth, they are classified in heading 8483 (8483.40) rather than 8482. Under 19 CFR 102.11(b), the toothed rings/races fail the 102.20 tariff shift and impart the essential character, conferring Chinese origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 1515
decisive_step: Cold pressing raw nuts and seeds into oils in Canada
flip: Cold press the oils in the United States and only bottle them in Canada
reasoning: Following precedent N351895, cold pressing raw nuts and seeds (Chapter 8 or 12) in Canada into fixed vegetable oils (Chapter 15, headings 1515/1515.11) satisfies the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3) (or 102.11(a)(1)/(a)(2) for Canadian-grown seeds), conferring Canadian origin.
